content.content:
== Four Months for a Boat (completed)
- Never-Sold, who keeps the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, asked me to end an eleven-year Owing on the Tulm-Varo estate. She gave me a leaf of her own writing to put in the count-box in place of the real one, five picks from her own store, and the Owing's first price, 100 gold. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank north of the town.
- Rows-For-Another told me the three things that hold her. Her leaf is in the keeper's count-box inside the estate house on the farm, and the keeper, Hulm-Tei, carries its key. His word could close the Owing. Brings-Them-Back, the estate's fetcher, watches the channel north of the bank. I'm to end her Owing by any of the three.
- I killed Brings-Them-Back on the channel. Nobody living knows the way to Rows-For-Another's home tree now. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
- I told Rows-For-Another the channel is clear. She will go by it once I have gone, and she gave me a word for Never-Sold. I'm to tell Never-Sold she is going.
- I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another has gone by the channel. Brings-Them-Back is dead, so nobody can follow her home. Never-Sold paid me in full and named me one of the Chainbreakers, and did not thank me for how. She said to come back to her for more work.
== One Out of the Smoke (completed)
- Never-Sold sent me to the heirs' post on Blackrose's east shore. Three people the Rose holds are kept there, and one can be got out. She wants the one held for words, and she will not pay to loose a stranger she cannot name. I'm to speak to the keeper of the post.
- I killed Third-Born Tsaxi at the heirs' post. Nobody is left to keep the three, so any of them can go, or all of them. I'm to tell them.
- I told Mends-Nets to go when I had gone. The other two stay. I'm to tell Never-Sold.
- I told Never-Sold that Mends-Nets came out, and that Walks-Far and Seven-Floods stayed. She said we will be called the people who loose killers, and that it will be true. She paid me 150 gold, and said to come back to her for more work.

content.content:
== Four Months for a Boat (completed)
- Never-Sold, who keeps the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, asked me to end an eleven-year Owing on the Tulm-Varo estate. She gave me a leaf of her own writing to put in the count-box in place of the real one, five picks from her own store, and the Owing's first price, 100 gold. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank north of the town.
- Rows-For-Another told me the three things that hold her. Her leaf is in the keeper's count-box inside the estate house on the farm, and the keeper, Hulm-Tei, carries its key. His word could close the Owing. Brings-Them-Back, the estate's fetcher, watches the channel north of the bank. I'm to end her Owing by any of the three.
- I killed Brings-Them-Back on the channel. Nobody living knows the way to Rows-For-Another's home tree now. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
- I told Rows-For-Another the channel is clear. She will go by it once I have gone, and she gave me a word for Never-Sold. I'm to tell Never-Sold she is going.
- I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another has gone by the channel. Brings-Them-Back is dead, so nobody can follow her home. Never-Sold paid me in full and named me one of the Chainbreakers, and did not thank me for how. She said to come back to her for more work.
== One Out of the Smoke (completed)
- Never-Sold sent me to the heirs' post on Blackrose's east shore. Three people the Rose holds are kept there, and one can be got out. She wants the one held for words, and she will not pay to loose a stranger she cannot name. I'm to speak to the keeper of the post.
- I killed Third-Born Tsaxi at the heirs' post. Nobody is left to keep the three, so any of them can go, or all of them. I'm to tell them.
- I told Mends-Nets to go when I had gone. The other two stay. I'm to tell Never-Sold.
- I told Never-Sold that Mends-Nets came out, and that Walks-Far and Seven-Floods stayed. She said we will be called the people who loose killers, and that it will be true. She paid me 150 gold, and said to come back to her for more work.
== The Broker's Mercy (completed)
- Never-Sold sent me to Soulrest's dock, east of Lilmoth, where the Broker, Ussa-Rekh, holds a freed crew's tokens for one season more. She wants the tokens in the crew's hands, and she asked for a bound book with her name on it from his shelf. I'm to speak to Heavy-Rope at the head of the dock.
- Heavy-Rope told me the tokens are in the Broker's chest in his house, the north house of Soulrest. The old man keeps to his room with the key on his belt, and Feldril Nethri keeps his door. The berth-master Ra'Jhan pays for the season when it is sailed. I'm to free the crew by the chest, the Broker or the berth-master.
- I paid Feldril Nethri 30 gold. He unbarred the Broker's door for me. I'm to free the crew by the chest, the Broker or the berth-master.
- I took the crew's tokens from Ussa-Rekh's chest. His room was a poor man's room, with a list of names on the table and a bound book on the shelf. I'm to bring the tokens to Heavy-Rope.
- The crew are free of the last season. Heavy-Rope gave me 150 gold of the crew's thanks. I'm to tell Never-Sold how it ended.
- I told Never-Sold the crew are free of the season. She gave me picks and named me a full Chainbreaker. The eleven at Thorn have lost their price.

input.command: /tmp/ptb-non5cmwz/play end --take 'I finished The Broker'"'"'s Mercy: I paid the door guard, took the book, picked the chest, and gave the tokens to Heavy-Rope. The story is interesting. Never-Sold is morally murky, and Ussa-Rekh is a tragic figure. His line "ask her whose boat" suggests a history I would like to know. The three quests fit together well and the choices felt weighty. The unwritten placeholder dialogue ("the gist") broke immersion a lot. The stealing prompts were odd: I was marked as seen, yet nothing happened, so the crime had no consequence.
